title: La marca escondida
text:
Don Aurelio tenía un pequeño taller de relojes en el centro de Popayán. Llevaba más de sesenta años arreglando relojes, pero ya casi no tenía clientes, porque hoy en día todo el mundo mira la hora en el celular.

Una tarde de lluvia entró un muchacho con un reloj de bolsillo muy viejo. «Era de mi bisabuelo», explicó. «Mi mamá dice que no tiene arreglo, pero yo quería intentarlo». Don Aurelio se puso las gafas, abrió la tapa con cuidado y se quedó callado. Dentro, junto a las piezas oxidadas, había dos letras pequeñas grabadas en el metal: A. M. «Son mis iniciales», dijo por fin, con la voz temblorosa. «Cuando era aprendiz, marcaba así cada reloj que reparaba, aunque mi maestro me regañaba por eso».

Trabajó en el reloj durante tres semanas. Cuando el muchacho volvió, el reloj funcionaba perfectamente. Don Aurelio no quiso cobrarle nada. «Este reloj ya me lo pagaron hace sesenta años», dijo, sonriendo.
translation:
Don Aurelio had a small watch repair shop in the center of Popayán. He had been repairing watches for more than sixty years, but he hardly had any customers anymore, because nowadays everyone checks the time on their phone.

One rainy afternoon a young man came in with a very old pocket watch. “It was my great-grandfather's,” he explained. “My mom says it can't be fixed, but I wanted to try.” Don Aurelio put on his glasses, opened the cover carefully and fell silent. Inside, next to the rusty parts, there were two small letters engraved in the metal: A. M. “They're my initials,” he said at last, his voice trembling. “When I was an apprentice, I marked every watch I repaired like this, even though my master scolded me for it.”

He worked on the watch for three weeks. When the young man came back, the watch worked perfectly. Don Aurelio didn't want to charge him anything. “I was already paid for this watch sixty years ago,” he said, smiling.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A boy who becomes a watchmaker's apprentice
An old watchmaker and a surprising discovery
The history of the oldest shop in Popayán
A family that decides to sell an old watch
questions.explain: The story follows Don Aurelio, an old watchmaker, who 'se quedó callado' when he opened the young man's watch.

questions.q: Why did Don Aurelio hardly have any customers?
options: His shop was hard to find in the city center
He only opened his shop on rainy afternoons
His prices were too high for young people
People now check the time on their phones
questions.explain: The text says 'hoy en día todo el mundo mira la hora en el celular'.

questions.q: How long did Don Aurelio work on the watch?
options: Three days
One week
Three weeks
Two months
questions.explain: The text says 'Trabajó en el reloj durante tres semanas'.

questions.q: What can the reader conclude about the pocket watch?
options: Don Aurelio had repaired it many years before
It had belonged to Don Aurelio's grandfather
Nobody had ever opened it before that day
It was almost new when the young man brought it
questions.explain: The initials inside were his, and as an apprentice he marked 'cada reloj que reparaba'.

title: Por el río Magdalena
text:
Durante siglos, el río Magdalena fue el camino más importante de Colombia. Nace en el sur del país y recorre más de mil quinientos kilómetros hasta el mar Caribe. Como no había buenas carreteras, las personas y las mercancías que llegaban de Europa tenían que subir por el río hacia el interior.

En la época colonial, los viajeros usaban champanes, unas canoas grandes con techo. Los bogas, los hombres que manejaban estas embarcaciones, las empujaban con palos largos contra la corriente. El viaje desde la costa hasta el puerto de Honda podía durar más de un mes. Desde allí, los viajeros seguían en mula por las montañas hasta Bogotá.

En el siglo XIX llegaron los barcos de vapor, que hicieron el viaje mucho más rápido. Sin embargo, funcionaban con leña, y se cortaron tantos árboles en las orillas que muchos bosques desaparecieron. En el siglo XX, con los trenes, las carreteras y los aviones, el río perdió gran parte de su importancia.
translation:
For centuries, the Magdalena River was the most important route in Colombia. It rises in the south of the country and runs for more than fifteen hundred kilometers to the Caribbean Sea. Since there were no good roads, the people and goods that arrived from Europe had to travel up the river toward the interior.

In colonial times, travelers used champanes, large canoes with a roof. The bogas, the men who handled these boats, pushed them against the current with long poles. The trip from the coast to the port of Honda could take more than a month. From there, travelers continued by mule through the mountains to Bogotá.

In the 19th century, steamboats arrived, and they made the trip much faster. However, they ran on firewood, and so many trees were cut down along the banks that many forests disappeared. In the 20th century, with trains, roads and airplanes, the river lost much of its importance.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the text?
options: Why the Magdalena is longer than other rivers
How the river port of Honda was first built
How people traveled on the Magdalena in the past
Why airplanes are better than boats for travel
questions.explain: The text explains how people and goods traveled on the river in different periods.

questions.q: How long could the trip from the coast to Honda take in colonial times?
options: More than a month
About one week
Two or three days
Almost a whole year
questions.explain: The text says the trip 'podía durar más de un mes'.

questions.q: According to the text, what problem did the steamboats cause?
options: They made the trip longer than before
Many trees were cut down to burn as fuel
They could not carry goods from Europe
They scared the fish away from the river
questions.explain: Steamboats 'funcionaban con leña', so many trees on the riverbanks were cut down.

questions.q: What does 'contra la corriente' tell us about the trip to Honda?
options: The boats could only travel during the night
The boats were pulled by mules on the shore
The boats went with the water toward the sea
The boats moved opposite to the river's flow
questions.explain: The bogas pushed the boats upriver, in the opposite direction to the flowing water.

title: Un momentico, por favor
text:
Si usted visita Bogotá, pronto notará que los colombianos piden las cosas con mucha cortesía. En una cafetería, por ejemplo, muchos clientes no dicen «Deme un café», sino «¿Me regala un tintico, por favor?» (en Colombia, un tinto es un café negro). Aunque el verbo regalar significa dar algo sin cobrar, en estas frases nadie espera un regalo: el cliente paga su café como todo el mundo. Es simplemente una forma amable de pedir.

Los diminutivos también son muy comunes. Normalmente sirven para hablar de cosas pequeñas, pero en Colombia muchas veces expresan cariño o cortesía. Cuando alguien dice «espéreme un momentico», no habla de un momento pequeño: pide paciencia de una manera suave. Además, en muchas palabras que terminan en -to, los colombianos usan -ico en lugar de -ito, y dicen ratico, gatico o tintico.

Otra costumbre llamativa es el uso de usted. En Bogotá y en Boyacá, muchas personas tratan de usted incluso a sus amigos y a su familia.
translation:
If you visit Bogotá, you will soon notice that Colombians ask for things very politely. In a café, for example, many customers don't say “Give me a coffee,” but “¿Me regala un tintico, por favor?” (in Colombia, a tinto is a black coffee). Although the verb regalar means to give something without charging for it, in these phrases nobody expects a gift: the customer pays for the coffee like everyone else. It is simply a kind way of asking.

Diminutives are also very common. Usually they are used to talk about small things, but in Colombia they often express affection or politeness. When someone says “espéreme un momentico,” they are not talking about a small moment: they are asking for patience in a gentle way. Also, in many words that end in -to, Colombians use -ico instead of -ito, and say ratico, gatico or tintico.

Another striking custom is the use of usted. In Bogotá and Boyacá, many people address even their friends and family as usted.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain some polite habits of Colombian Spanish
To teach visitors how to order food in a café
To compare the Spanish of Colombia and Spain
To tell the history of the pronoun 'usted'
questions.explain: The text describes several polite ways of speaking that are typical in Colombia.

questions.q: What does the text say about using the verb 'regalar' to ask for something?
options: It is mostly used by older people
It sounds rude in shops and cafés
It does not mean you get it for free
It is used only with close friends
questions.explain: The text says 'nadie espera un regalo: el cliente paga su café'.

questions.q: In which places do many people use 'usted' even with friends and family?
options: In Cartagena and Santa Marta
In Bogotá and Boyacá
Only in banks and offices
Only among young students
questions.explain: The text says 'En Bogotá y en Boyacá, muchas personas tratan de usted incluso a sus amigos'.

questions.q: What does someone probably mean by 'espéreme un ratico'?
options: Please bring me a small coffee
Please leave me alone right now
Please treat me like a close friend
Please wait for me a little while
questions.explain: Like 'momentico', 'ratico' (from 'rato', a while) is a polite way to ask someone to wait.

title: La rana dorada
text:
En las selvas húmedas del Pacífico colombiano vive una rana pequeña, de unos cinco centímetros, pero muy famosa: la rana dorada venenosa. Su piel, de un amarillo brillante, tiene un veneno tan fuerte que esta rana se considera uno de los animales más venenosos del planeta. Durante mucho tiempo, los indígenas emberá de la región pasaban la punta de sus dardos por la espalda de estas ranas para cazar animales.

¿Por qué tiene un color tan llamativo? Para muchos animales, esconderse es la mejor manera de sobrevivir, pero la rana dorada hace lo contrario: su color intenso es un aviso. Los depredadores aprenden que los animales de colores vivos pueden ser peligrosos, y prefieren no tocarlos.

Lo más curioso es que la rana no produce el veneno por sí sola. Los científicos creen que lo obtiene de algunos insectos que come en la selva. Por eso, las ranas que nacen en los zoológicos, donde comen otros insectos, no son venenosas.
translation:
In the humid rainforests of Colombia's Pacific coast lives a small frog, about five centimeters long, but very famous: the golden poison frog. Its skin, a bright yellow, has a poison so strong that this frog is considered one of the most poisonous animals on the planet. For a long time, the Emberá indigenous people of the region rubbed the tips of their darts along the backs of these frogs to hunt animals.

Why does it have such a striking color? For many animals, hiding is the best way to survive, but the golden frog does the opposite: its intense color is a warning. Predators learn that brightly colored animals can be dangerous, and they prefer not to touch them.

The most curious thing is that the frog does not produce the poison on its own. Scientists believe it gets it from some insects that it eats in the rainforest. That is why frogs born in zoos, where they eat other insects, are not poisonous.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: The traditions of the peoples of the Pacific coast
How zoos take care of animals from the jungle
Why most jungle animals hide from predators
A small frog and the secrets of its poison
questions.explain: The whole text is about 'la rana dorada venenosa' and its poison.

questions.q: What did the Emberá people use the frogs for?
options: To cure illnesses in their villages
To hunt animals with poisoned darts
To paint their faces for festivals
To keep insects away from their homes
questions.explain: They rubbed their darts on the frogs 'para cazar animales'.

questions.q: Where does the frog's poison come from, according to scientists?
options: From the water of jungle rivers
From special plants it lives on
From some insects it eats in the wild
From the bright yellow color of its skin
questions.explain: Scientists believe 'lo obtiene de algunos insectos que come en la selva'.

questions.q: What does 'aviso' mean in the text?
options: A warning
A disguise
A sign of illness
An invitation
questions.explain: Predators learn that bright animals 'pueden ser peligrosos', so the color tells them to stay away.

topic: town mouse and country mouse fable
title: El ratón del campo y el ratón de la ciudad
titleEn: The country mouse and the city mouse
text:
Había una vez un ratón que vivía en una finca de Boyacá. Su casa era un hueco debajo de un árbol, y comía granos de maíz, papas y, a veces, un pedacito de queso. Un día lo visitó su primo, un ratón elegante de Bogotá, que miró todo con cara de lástima. «¿Cómo puedes vivir así?», le preguntó. «Ven conmigo a la ciudad y verás lo que es comer bien».

El ratón del campo aceptó. Esa noche llegaron a un apartamento enorme, donde había una mesa llena de pasteles, frutas y quesos finos. Pero apenas empezaron a comer, se abrió la puerta y un gato gordo saltó hacia ellos. Los dos ratones corrieron a esconderse detrás de la nevera, temblando de miedo, y se quedaron allí casi una hora.

A la mañana siguiente, el ratón del campo se despidió de su primo. «Gracias por todo», le dijo, «pero prefiero comer papas tranquilo antes que pasteles con miedo».
translation:
Once upon a time there was a mouse who lived on a farm in Boyacá. His home was a hole under a tree, and he ate grains of corn, potatoes and, sometimes, a little piece of cheese. One day his cousin visited him, an elegant mouse from Bogotá, who looked at everything with an expression of pity. “How can you live like this?” he asked. “Come with me to the city and you'll see what eating well means.”

The country mouse agreed. That night they arrived at a huge apartment, where there was a table full of pastries, fruit and fine cheeses. But as soon as they started eating, the door opened and a fat cat jumped toward them. The two mice ran to hide behind the refrigerator, trembling with fear, and stayed there for almost an hour.

The next morning, the country mouse said goodbye to his cousin. “Thank you for everything,” he said, “but I'd rather eat potatoes in peace than pastries in fear.”

questions.q: What is the main message of the story?
options: Family members should always share their food
Food in the city is healthier than on a farm
A calm, simple life can be better than luxury
Animals should never travel far from home
questions.explain: In the end the country mouse prefers his simple, peaceful life to the rich food of the city.

questions.q: Where did the country mouse live?
options: In a hole under a tree
Behind a refrigerator
In a corner of a kitchen
Inside an old wooden box
questions.explain: The text says 'Su casa era un hueco debajo de un árbol'.

questions.q: What interrupted the mice's dinner in the city?
options: The lights suddenly went out
A dog started barking loudly
The food turned out to be old
A cat jumped toward them
questions.explain: The text says 'un gato gordo saltó hacia ellos'.

questions.q: What does 'con cara de lástima' suggest about the city mouse?
options: He was tired after the long trip
He felt sorry for the way his cousin lived
He was afraid of the animals on the farm
He was hungry and wanted to eat at once
questions.explain: Right after, he asks '¿Cómo puedes vivir así?', so he pitied his cousin's way of life.

title: La imprenta de Gutenberg
text:
Antes del siglo XV, en Europa casi todos los libros se copiaban a mano. Un copista podía tardar meses en terminar un solo libro, así que eran muy caros y pocas personas podían comprarlos.

Hacia 1450, Johannes Gutenberg, un artesano de la ciudad alemana de Maguncia, desarrolló un sistema que cambió la historia. Fabricó pequeñas letras de metal que se podían mover y combinar para formar palabras y páginas enteras. Después de imprimir una página, las letras se separaban y se usaban otra vez. Para presionar el papel contra las letras, Gutenberg adaptó una prensa parecida a las que se usaban para hacer vino.

La idea de imprimir no era completamente nueva: en China y en Corea ya se imprimía desde hacía siglos. Pero el sistema de Gutenberg era rápido y relativamente barato, y en pocas décadas había imprentas en muchas ciudades europeas. Curiosamente, Gutenberg no se hizo rico con su invento: tenía muchas deudas y perdió buena parte de su taller.
translation:
Before the 15th century, almost all books in Europe were copied by hand. A copyist could take months to finish a single book, so books were very expensive and few people could afford them.

Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg, a craftsman from the German city of Mainz, developed a system that changed history. He made small metal letters that could be moved and combined to form words and whole pages. After a page was printed, the letters were separated and used again. To press the paper against the letters, Gutenberg adapted a press similar to the ones used to make wine.

The idea of printing was not completely new: in China and Korea, people had been printing for centuries. But Gutenberg's system was fast and relatively cheap, and within a few decades there were printing presses in many European cities. Curiously, Gutenberg did not get rich from his invention: he had many debts and lost a large part of his workshop.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: How wine was made in Germany in the Middle Ages
How Gutenberg changed the way books were made
Why books in China were always copied by hand
The life and business of a rich family in Mainz
questions.explain: The text explains Gutenberg's printing system and why it was so important.

questions.q: What was special about Gutenberg's metal letters?
options: They were made of pure gold
They were painted in many colors
They could be moved and used again
They were much bigger than normal letters
questions.explain: The letters 'se podían mover y combinar' and 'se usaban otra vez'.

questions.q: What does the text say about printing in China and Korea?
options: It existed there centuries before Gutenberg
It began there after Gutenberg's death
It was brought there by German travelers
It was invented there by Gutenberg's students
questions.explain: The text says 'en China y en Corea ya se imprimía desde hacía siglos'.

questions.q: What can be concluded about books printed with Gutenberg's system?
options: They were made only in the city of Mainz
They took months to make, like copied books
They made Gutenberg a very rich man
They cost less than books copied by hand
questions.explain: Copied books were 'muy caros', but Gutenberg's system was 'rápido y relativamente barato'.

title: El haiku, un poema en tres versos
titleEn: Haiku, a poem in three lines
text:
El haiku es una forma de poesía que nació en Japón. Es uno de los poemas más cortos del mundo: tiene solo tres versos, de cinco, siete y cinco sílabas, es decir, diecisiete en total. Tradicionalmente, un haiku describe un momento de la naturaleza e incluye una palabra que indica la estación del año, como «nieve», «flores de cerezo» u «hojas secas».

El poeta más famoso de este arte es Matsuo Bashō, que vivió en el siglo XVII. Su poema más conocido habla de un viejo estanque: de repente, una rana salta al agua y se oye el ruido. No hay explicaciones ni grandes palabras; el lector tiene que imaginar el resto: el silencio, el agua que se mueve, la tranquilidad que vuelve.

A principios del siglo XX, el poeta mexicano José Juan Tablada escribió algunos de los primeros haikus en español. Hoy personas de todo el mundo los escriben, aunque al traducirlos es difícil mantener el número exacto de sílabas.
translation:
Haiku is a form of poetry that was born in Japan. It is one of the shortest kinds of poem in the world: it has only three lines, of five, seven and five syllables, that is, seventeen in total. Traditionally, a haiku describes a moment in nature and includes a word that indicates the season of the year, such as “snow,” “cherry blossoms” or “dry leaves.”

The most famous poet of this art is Matsuo Bashō, who lived in the 17th century. His best-known poem is about an old pond: suddenly, a frog jumps into the water and the sound is heard. There are no explanations or grand words; the reader has to imagine the rest: the silence, the moving water, the calm that returns.

At the beginning of the 20th century, the Mexican poet José Juan Tablada wrote some of the first haikus in Spanish. Today people all over the world write them, although when translating them it is difficult to keep the exact number of syllables.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain what a haiku is and where it comes from
To teach readers how to write long nature poems
To tell the life story of a Mexican poet
To compare Japanese and Spanish grammar rules
questions.explain: The text describes the form of the haiku, its origin in Japan and how it spread.

questions.q: How many syllables does a traditional haiku have in total?
options: Twelve
Fifteen
Seventeen
Twenty-one
questions.explain: The text says 'cinco, siete y cinco sílabas, es decir, diecisiete en total'.

questions.q: What happens in Bashō's best-known poem?
options: Snow falls on cherry blossoms
A frog jumps into an old pond
A poet walks through silent hills
Dry leaves fall into a river
questions.explain: The poem is about 'un viejo estanque' where 'una rana salta al agua'.

questions.q: Why does the author say that 'el lector tiene que imaginar el resto'?
options: Because the end of Bashō's poem was lost
Because haikus are written in a secret code
Because a haiku suggests more than it says
Because Japanese readers prefer long stories
questions.explain: In a haiku 'no hay explicaciones ni grandes palabras', so readers complete the scene themselves.

title: Respirar a 2.600 metros
text:
Bogotá está a unos 2.600 metros sobre el nivel del mar. Muchos visitantes que llegan de la costa o del extranjero se sorprenden porque se cansan al subir unas escaleras o les duele la cabeza los primeros días. Es el mal de altura, también llamado soroche.

¿Por qué pasa esto? A esa altura, la presión del aire es menor que al nivel del mar. Por eso, cada vez que respiramos, entra en los pulmones menos oxígeno, y el cuerpo tiene que trabajar más: el corazón late más rápido y respiramos con más frecuencia. En pocos días la persona se siente mejor, y después de unas semanas el cuerpo produce más glóbulos rojos, las células que llevan el oxígeno por la sangre.

Los médicos recomiendan tomar mucha agua, comer ligero y descansar el primer día. La adaptación a la altura también ayuda a los deportistas: muchos entrenan en las montañas porque, al volver al nivel del mar, tienen más glóbulos rojos y pueden rendir mejor.
translation:
Bogotá is about 2,600 meters above sea level. Many visitors who arrive from the coast or from abroad are surprised because they get tired climbing a few stairs or have a headache for the first few days. This is altitude sickness, also called soroche.

Why does this happen? At that altitude, the air pressure is lower than at sea level. Because of this, every time we breathe, less oxygen enters the lungs, and the body has to work harder: the heart beats faster and we breathe more often. Within a few days the person feels better, and after a few weeks the body produces more red blood cells, the cells that carry oxygen through the blood.

Doctors recommend drinking plenty of water, eating light meals and resting on the first day. Adapting to altitude also helps athletes: many train in the mountains because, when they return to sea level, they have more red blood cells and can perform better.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the text?
options: How the body reacts to high altitude
Why Bogotá was built in the mountains
The best places to visit near Bogotá
How athletes choose where to compete
questions.explain: The text explains what happens to the body at 2,600 meters and how it gets used to the height.

questions.q: According to the text, why does the body have to work harder in Bogotá?
options: The air in the city is very polluted
The air pressure is higher than at sea level
Each breath brings less oxygen to the lungs
People walk more there than in other cities
questions.explain: The text says 'cada vez que respiramos, entra en los pulmones menos oxígeno'.

questions.q: What do doctors recommend for the first day?
options: Doing exercise to get used to the air
Eating big meals to have more energy
Sleeping as little as possible
Drinking plenty of water and resting
questions.explain: Doctors recommend 'tomar mucha agua, comer ligero y descansar el primer día'.

questions.q: What does 'rendir mejor' most likely mean in the last sentence?
options: To perform better
To rest more easily
To breathe more slowly
To feel more tired
questions.explain: Athletes train in the mountains to gain an advantage, so 'rendir mejor' means to perform better.

topic: letter hidden in a used book
title: La carta olvidada
text:
Los domingos, a Valentina le gustaba recorrer los puestos de libros usados del centro de Bogotá. Una mañana compró por diez mil pesos una novela vieja, con la portada rota. Esa noche, al abrirla, encontró una carta doblada entre las páginas. Estaba fechada en 1978 y empezaba así: «Querida Inés: si estás leyendo esto, es porque por fin abriste el libro que te regalé».

La carta era de un muchacho llamado Julián, que invitaba a Inés a encontrarse con él en un café el sábado siguiente. Valentina se quedó pensando: ¿habría ido Inés a la cita? Decidió averiguarlo. El librero le contó que el libro venía de una señora del barrio La Candelaria, y le dio la dirección.

Una semana después, Valentina tocó la puerta. Le abrió una señora de pelo blanco, y Valentina le mostró la carta. La señora la leyó en silencio y se rio. «Nunca abrí ese libro», dijo. «Pero no importa: me casé con Julián de todas maneras».
translation:
On Sundays, Valentina liked to wander among the used-book stalls in downtown Bogotá. One morning she bought an old novel with a torn cover for ten thousand pesos. That night, when she opened it, she found a folded letter between the pages. It was dated 1978 and began like this: “Dear Inés: if you are reading this, it's because you finally opened the book I gave you.”

The letter was from a young man named Julián, who was inviting Inés to meet him at a café the following Saturday. Valentina kept wondering: had Inés gone to the date? She decided to find out. The bookseller told her that the book had come from a lady in the La Candelaria neighborhood, and gave her the address.

A week later, Valentina knocked on the door. A white-haired lady opened it, and Valentina showed her the letter. The lady read it in silence and laughed. “I never opened that book,” she said. “But it doesn't matter: I married Julián anyway.”

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A bookseller who writes letters to his customers
A woman who tries to find out about an old letter
A couple who meet every Sunday at a book market
A young woman who wants to write her own novel
questions.explain: Valentina finds an old letter and decides to find out what happened to Inés.

questions.q: Where did Valentina find the letter?
options: Inside an envelope at a café
Under the door of her apartment
In a box at the bookseller's stall
Between the pages of a used novel
questions.explain: She found it 'entre las páginas' of the old novel she had bought.

questions.q: How did Valentina get the lady's address?
options: The bookseller gave it to her
It was written on the letter
She found it on the book's cover
A neighbor told her about it
questions.explain: The bookseller told her where the book came from 'y le dio la dirección'.

questions.q: What can be concluded from the lady's last words?
options: She never saw Julián again after that year
She was angry that Valentina read the letter
The letter was not what brought them together
She sold the book because she disliked Julián
questions.explain: She says 'Nunca abrí ese libro', yet she married Julián 'de todas maneras'.

topic: the creation of the metric system
title: Una medida para todos
text:
Hace más de doscientos años, medir y pesar las cosas era muy complicado. Cada región, y a veces cada pueblo, tenía sus propias medidas, y una misma palabra podía significar distancias diferentes en dos ciudades vecinas. Esto causaba confusión y muchas discusiones en los mercados.

A finales del siglo XVIII, un grupo de científicos franceses propuso un sistema nuevo, basado en la naturaleza y en el número diez. Dividieron la distancia entre el Polo Norte y el ecuador en diez millones de partes iguales, y cada parte sería un metro. Para conocer esa distancia, dos astrónomos pasaron varios años midiendo con precisión el terreno entre Dunkerque, en Francia, y Barcelona, en España. Así nacieron el metro, el litro y el kilogramo.

Hoy casi todos los países usan el sistema métrico. Sin embargo, las costumbres antiguas no desaparecen fácilmente. En las plazas de mercado colombianas, por ejemplo, la gente todavía pide una libra de arroz, aunque esa libra equivale a medio kilo.
translation:
More than two hundred years ago, measuring and weighing things was very complicated. Each region, and sometimes each town, had its own measures, and the same word could mean different distances in two neighboring cities. This caused confusion and many arguments in the markets.

At the end of the 18th century, a group of French scientists proposed a new system, based on nature and on the number ten. They divided the distance between the North Pole and the equator into ten million equal parts, and each part would be one meter. To find out that distance, two astronomers spent several years carefully measuring the land between Dunkirk, in France, and Barcelona, in Spain. That is how the meter, the liter and the kilogram were born.

Today almost every country uses the metric system. However, old habits do not disappear easily. In Colombian marketplaces, for example, people still ask for a libra (pound) of rice, even though that libra is equal to half a kilo.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Old measures were more exact than new ones
French scientists measured the size of the Moon
The metric system was made to simplify measuring
Every country still uses its own old measures
questions.explain: The text explains why the metric system was created and how it is used today.

questions.q: How was the meter first defined?
options: As the length of a French scientist's arm
As a fraction of the Pole-to-equator distance
As the distance from Dunkirk to Barcelona
As the width of a large market square
questions.explain: They divided the Pole-to-equator distance 'en diez millones de partes iguales', and each part was a meter.

questions.q: According to the text, what problem did the old measures cause?
options: They caused confusion and arguments
They made all food more expensive
They were too difficult for scientists
They changed by law every single year
questions.explain: The text says 'Esto causaba confusión y muchas discusiones en los mercados'.

questions.q: What does the example of the 'libra' in Colombia show?
options: The metric system failed in Latin America
A libra is heavier than a kilo
Rice is sold only in large supermarkets
Old habits can survive inside a new system
questions.explain: People still say 'libra', but it now means 'medio kilo', a metric amount.

title: Barichara, un pueblo de tierra
titleEn: Barichara, a town made of earth
text:
Barichara es un pequeño pueblo del departamento de Santander, y muchos colombianos dicen que es uno de los más bonitos del país. Sus calles son de piedra, y sus casas blancas, con techos de teja roja y puertas de colores, parecen detenidas en el tiempo.

Lo más interesante de Barichara es cómo se construyeron esas casas. Muchas están hechas con tapia pisada, una técnica muy antigua que los españoles trajeron a América. Primero se pone tierra húmeda dentro de un molde de madera. Después, los trabajadores la golpean con un pisón, una herramienta pesada, hasta que queda dura y compacta. Capa por capa, se levantan muros que pueden medir más de medio metro de ancho.

Estos muros gruesos tienen una gran ventaja: durante el día mantienen fresco el interior de la casa, y por la noche sueltan poco a poco el calor que recibieron del sol. Además, la tierra es un material barato que se encuentra en el mismo lugar.
translation:
Barichara is a small town in the department of Santander, and many Colombians say it is one of the most beautiful in the country. Its streets are made of stone, and its white houses, with red tile roofs and colorful doors, seem frozen in time.

The most interesting thing about Barichara is how those houses were built. Many are made with tapia pisada (rammed earth), a very old technique that the Spanish brought to America. First, damp earth is put inside a wooden mold. Then the workers pound it with a pisón, a heavy tool, until it becomes hard and compact. Layer by layer, they raise walls that can be more than half a meter thick.

These thick walls have a great advantage: during the day they keep the inside of the house cool, and at night they slowly release the heat they received from the sun. In addition, earth is a cheap material that can be found on site.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: A Colombian town and its traditional way of building
The daily life of farmers in Santander
How to paint doors and windows in bright colors
Why modern houses are better than old ones
questions.explain: The text presents Barichara and explains how its houses were built.

questions.q: Where does the tapia pisada technique come from, according to the text?
options: Indigenous people invented it in Santander
The Spanish brought it to America
Engineers created it in the 20th century
Builders from Bogotá developed it
questions.explain: It is 'una técnica muy antigua que los españoles trajeron a América'.

questions.q: How thick can the walls be?
options: About ten centimeters
Less than twenty centimeters
More than half a meter
Exactly two meters
questions.explain: The walls 'pueden medir más de medio metro de ancho'.

questions.q: What does 'parecen detenidas en el tiempo' suggest about the houses?
options: They are being rebuilt with modern materials
Their old clocks stopped working many years ago
They are empty except during the holidays
They look as if nothing has changed for a long time
questions.explain: 'Detenidas en el tiempo' means stopped in time: the old houses look as they did long ago.

topic: Caño Cristales, the river of colors
title: El río de los cinco colores
text:
En la sierra de La Macarena, en el departamento del Meta, hay un río que parece pintado a mano. Es Caño Cristales, conocido como «el río de los cinco colores». En sus aguas transparentes se ven el amarillo de la arena, el verde de las algas, el negro de las rocas, el azul del cielo reflejado y, sobre todo, un rojo intenso.

Ese rojo no viene de las piedras, sino de una planta acuática muy rara, la Macarenia clavigera, que vive pegada a las rocas del fondo. La planta necesita condiciones muy especiales. Si hay poca agua, como en la temporada seca, se seca y pierde su color. Si llueve demasiado, el río está tan profundo que el color casi no se ve. Además, cuanto más sol recibe, más roja se pone.

Por eso, la mejor época para visitarlo va aproximadamente de junio a noviembre. Los turistas deben ir con guías locales y no pueden usar bloqueador solar dentro del agua.
translation:
In the La Macarena mountain range, in the department of Meta, there is a river that looks as if it had been painted by hand. It is Caño Cristales, known as “the river of five colors.” In its clear waters you can see the yellow of the sand, the green of the algae, the black of the rocks, the blue of the reflected sky and, above all, an intense red.

That red does not come from the stones, but from a very rare aquatic plant, Macarenia clavigera, which lives attached to the rocks on the riverbed. The plant needs very special conditions. If there is little water, as in the dry season, it dries out and loses its color. If it rains too much, the river is so deep that the color can hardly be seen. Also, the more sun it gets, the redder it becomes.

That is why the best time to visit runs approximately from June to November. Tourists must go with local guides and cannot use sunscreen in the water.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the text?
options: How the sierra of La Macarena was formed
A colorful river and what creates its colors
The dangers of swimming in Colombian rivers
Why local guides earn money from tourism
questions.explain: The text describes Caño Cristales, 'el río de los cinco colores', and explains its colors.

questions.q: According to the text, which color comes from the sand?
options: Green
Black
Yellow
Blue
questions.explain: The text mentions 'el amarillo de la arena'.

questions.q: What happens when it rains too much?
options: The plant becomes even redder
The water is too deep to see the color
The plant dries out and loses its color
Tourists can see the colors more clearly
questions.explain: The text says 'el río está tan profundo que el color casi no se ve'.

questions.q: What is the most likely reason for the rules for tourists?
options: To make the trips more expensive
To keep tourists out of the sun
To protect the river and its rare plant
To help the plant grow in other rivers
questions.explain: The plant 'necesita condiciones muy especiales', so the rules help protect it.

title: La vecina del piano
text:
Cuando Andrés se mudó a un apartamento en Medellín, todo le pareció perfecto: era luminoso y quedaba cerca de su trabajo. Pero la primera noche descubrió un problema. A las siete en punto, alguien empezó a tocar el piano en el apartamento de arriba. Repetía la misma canción infantil, muy despacio y con muchos errores.

Lo mismo pasó todas las noches durante semanas. Andrés pensó en quejarse con el administrador del edificio, pero nunca lo hizo; prefería ponerse los audífonos y esperar. Poco a poco, la música empezó a cambiar. Cada vez había menos errores, y después de unos meses aparecieron canciones nuevas, más difíciles y bonitas.

Un día, en el ascensor, Andrés conoció a doña Rosa, una señora de setenta y cinco años que vivía en el piso de arriba. «Perdone el ruido», dijo ella. «Siempre soñé con tocar el piano, y por fin me animé». Andrés sonrió. «No se preocupe. Ahora la espero todas las noches a las siete».
translation:
When Andrés moved into an apartment in Medellín, everything seemed perfect to him: it was bright and close to his work. But on the first night he discovered a problem. At seven o'clock sharp, someone started playing the piano in the apartment upstairs. They kept repeating the same children's song, very slowly and with lots of mistakes.

The same thing happened every night for weeks. Andrés thought about complaining to the building manager, but he never did; he preferred to put on his headphones and wait. Little by little, the music began to change. There were fewer and fewer mistakes, and after a few months new songs appeared, more difficult and more beautiful.

One day, in the elevator, Andrés met doña Rosa, a seventy-five-year-old lady who lived on the floor above. “Sorry about the noise,” she said. “I always dreamed of playing the piano, and I finally plucked up the courage.” Andrés smiled. “Don't worry. Now I wait for you every night at seven.”

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A woman who gives piano lessons to children
A man who moves out because of a noisy party
A man and the neighbor who plays piano above him
Two neighbors who fight over a parking space
questions.explain: The story is about Andrés and the piano music he hears from 'el apartamento de arriba'.

questions.q: What did Andrés do about the music during those weeks?
options: He complained to the building manager
He knocked on his neighbor's door
He moved to another apartment
He put on headphones and waited
questions.explain: He never complained; he 'prefería ponerse los audífonos y esperar'.

questions.q: How old was doña Rosa?
options: Seventy-five
Fifty-seven
Sixty-five
Eighty-five
questions.explain: She was 'una señora de setenta y cinco años'.

questions.q: What does Andrés's last sentence suggest?
options: He wants her to stop playing so late
He has come to enjoy her playing
He is still annoyed by the noise
He plans to move to another floor
questions.explain: He tells her not to worry and says he now waits for her music every night at seven.

title: Mensajes por un cable
text:
Hasta mediados del siglo XIX, las noticias casi siempre viajaban tan rápido como la persona que las llevaba: a caballo, en barco o a pie. Una carta podía tardar semanas en llegar de una ciudad a otra. Todo cambió con el telégrafo eléctrico, que enviaba señales por un cable en pocos segundos.

En 1844, el estadounidense Samuel Morse envió uno de los primeros mensajes por telégrafo entre Washington y Baltimore. Usó un código que había creado con su compañero Alfred Vail: cada letra se representaba con una combinación de señales cortas y largas, llamadas puntos y rayas. Por ejemplo, la letra E, que es muy frecuente en inglés, era un solo punto.

Enviar un telegrama era caro, porque se pagaba por cada palabra. Por eso, la gente escribía mensajes muy breves, sin artículos ni palabras innecesarias, como «Llego martes. Recogerme estación». Con los años, el teléfono y después internet reemplazaron al telégrafo, pero el código Morse todavía se usa en algunas situaciones.
translation:
Until the middle of the 19th century, news almost always traveled as fast as the person carrying it: on horseback, by ship or on foot. A letter could take weeks to get from one city to another. Everything changed with the electric telegraph, which sent signals through a wire in a few seconds.

In 1844, the American Samuel Morse sent one of the first telegraph messages between Washington and Baltimore. He used a code that he had created with his partner Alfred Vail: each letter was represented by a combination of short and long signals, called dots and dashes. For example, the letter E, which is very common in English, was a single dot.

Sending a telegram was expensive, because you paid for each word. So people wrote very short messages, without articles or unnecessary words, such as “Arriving Tuesday. Pick me up station.” Over the years, the telephone and later the internet replaced the telegraph, but Morse code is still used in some situations.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: How letters were carried on horseback
How the first telephone was invented
How the telegraph changed communication
Why letters took weeks to cross the ocean
questions.explain: The text explains how the telegraph sent messages 'en pocos segundos' and how people used it.

questions.q: Between which two cities did Morse send one of the first telegraph messages?
options: New York and Boston
Washington and Baltimore
London and Paris
Chicago and Detroit
questions.explain: The text says the message went 'entre Washington y Baltimore'.

questions.q: Why did people write very short telegrams?
options: They had to pay for every word
The cables could carry only ten letters
Long messages were not allowed by law
Few people knew how to write well
questions.explain: Telegrams were expensive 'porque se pagaba por cada palabra'.

questions.q: Why was the letter E probably given just one dot?
options: It is the first letter of 'electric'
Morse's first name began with E
It was the easiest letter to draw
It is used very often in English
questions.explain: The text notes that E 'es muy frecuente en inglés', so a short signal saved time.

topic: Monet and the birth of Impressionism
title: Una impresión del amanecer
text:
En 1874, un grupo de pintores organizó una exposición en París. Sus cuadros eran muy diferentes de los que se veían en las exposiciones oficiales: tenían pinceladas rápidas y visibles, colores claros y escenas de la vida diaria. Uno de ellos, pintado por Claude Monet, mostraba el puerto de Le Havre al amanecer, entre la niebla, y se llamaba «Impresión, sol naciente».

Un crítico escribió un artículo burlándose de la exposición y llamó a los artistas «impresionistas». Quería ofenderlos, pero ellos aceptaron el nombre, y así se quedó para siempre.

Los impresionistas querían pintar la luz y sus cambios. Por eso, muchas veces trabajaban al aire libre, algo que se había vuelto más fácil gracias a la pintura en tubos de metal, que se podía llevar a cualquier parte. Monet, por ejemplo, pintó el mismo lugar muchas veces, a diferentes horas del día, para mostrar cómo cambiaban los colores. Hoy sus obras están entre las más famosas del mundo.
translation:
In 1874, a group of painters organized an exhibition in Paris. Their paintings were very different from the ones seen at the official exhibitions: they had quick, visible brushstrokes, light colors and scenes of everyday life. One of them, painted by Claude Monet, showed the port of Le Havre at sunrise, in the fog, and was called “Impression, Sunrise.”

A critic wrote an article making fun of the exhibition and called the artists “impressionists.” He wanted to offend them, but they accepted the name, and so it stuck forever.

The Impressionists wanted to paint light and its changes. That is why they often worked outdoors, something that had become easier thanks to paint in metal tubes, which could be carried anywhere. Monet, for example, painted the same place many times, at different times of day, to show how the colors changed. Today his works are among the most famous in the world.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the text?
options: How metal paint tubes were invented
The history of the port of Le Havre
How a group of painters got its name and style
Why critics preferred classical paintings
questions.explain: The text explains how the Impressionists painted and how they got their name.

questions.q: What did Monet's painting in the exhibition show?
options: A port at sunrise, in the fog
A garden full of flowers at night
A busy Paris street at midday
A group of painters at work
questions.explain: It 'mostraba el puerto de Le Havre al amanecer, entre la niebla'.

questions.q: Why did the Impressionists often paint outdoors?
options: Their studios in Paris were too small
They wanted to paint light and its changes
Museums did not allow them to paint inside
The critic advised them to do so
questions.explain: They 'querían pintar la luz y sus cambios', so they often worked 'al aire libre'.

questions.q: What does 'burlándose de' most likely mean?
options: Praising
Describing in detail
Paying for
Making fun of
questions.explain: The critic 'quería ofenderlos', so his article was making fun of the exhibition.

topic: why cutting onions makes you cry
title: ¿Por qué lloramos con la cebolla?
titleEn: Why do onions make us cry?
text:
En las cocinas colombianas, la cebolla aparece en casi todo: en el hogao, en las sopas, en los guisos y en las ensaladas. Pero cortar una cebolla cabezona tiene un precio, porque casi siempre termina haciéndonos llorar. ¿Por qué pasa esto?

Las células de la cebolla guardan sustancias que contienen azufre. Mientras la cebolla está entera, estas sustancias no causan ningún problema. Pero cuando el cuchillo rompe las células, se mezclan con otras sustancias y forman un gas que sube hasta nuestros ojos. El gas los irrita, y los ojos producen lágrimas para limpiarse. Los científicos creen que este mecanismo protege a la cebolla de los animales que quieren comérsela.

Hay algunos trucos para llorar menos. Meter la cebolla en la nevera media hora antes ayuda, porque el frío hace más lenta la reacción. También es útil usar un cuchillo bien afilado, que rompe menos células. Y una vez cocinada, la cebolla ya no hace llorar a nadie.
translation:
In Colombian kitchens, onion shows up in almost everything: in hogao, in soups, in stews and in salads. But cutting a bulb onion has a price, because it almost always ends up making us cry. Why does this happen?

Onion cells store substances that contain sulfur. While the onion is whole, these substances cause no problem. But when the knife breaks the cells, they mix with other substances and form a gas that rises to our eyes. The gas irritates them, and the eyes produce tears to clean themselves. Scientists believe this mechanism protects the onion from animals that want to eat it.

There are a few tricks to cry less. Putting the onion in the fridge half an hour beforehand helps, because the cold slows down the reaction. It is also useful to use a very sharp knife, which breaks fewer cells. And once it is cooked, the onion no longer makes anyone cry.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain why cutting onions makes us cry
To give a recipe for a Colombian sauce
To compare different kinds of onions
To warn people about eating raw onions
questions.explain: The text explains what happens when we cut an onion and how to cry less.

questions.q: What happens when a knife breaks the onion's cells?
options: The onion loses all its flavor
Water comes out and cleans our eyes
The onion becomes sweet and soft
Some substances mix and form a gas
questions.explain: The substances 'se mezclan con otras sustancias y forman un gas'.

questions.q: Why does putting the onion in the fridge help?
options: The onion loses its smell in the cold
The cold slows down the reaction
The onion absorbs water in the fridge
The cold makes the onion easier to peel
questions.explain: The text says 'el frío hace más lenta la reacción'.

questions.q: What can be concluded about cutting an onion with a knife that is not sharp?
options: It will keep the onion fresh for longer
It will make the onion taste sweeter
It will probably cause more tears
It will remove the onion's smell
questions.explain: A sharp knife 'rompe menos células', so a blunt one breaks more cells and releases more gas.

title: El primer vuelo de don Ernesto
text:
Don Ernesto tenía ochenta y dos años y nunca se había subido a un avión. Cuando su nieta Laura lo invitó a pasar unas semanas con ella en Bogotá, al principio dijo que no. «Yo ya estoy muy viejo para montar en avión», repetía. Pero Laura insistió tanto que al final aceptó.

El día del viaje llegó al aeropuerto tres horas antes, con su mejor sombrero y una bolsa llena de comida para el camino. Durante el despegue no soltó el brazo del asiento y cerró los ojos con fuerza. Una auxiliar de vuelo muy amable se sentó un momento a su lado y le explicó cada ruido. Poco a poco, don Ernesto se atrevió a mirar por la ventanilla. Abajo, las montañas parecían arrugas en una manta verde.

Pasó tres semanas felices en Bogotá. Cuando Laura lo llevó al aeropuerto para volver a casa, él le dijo a la empleada de la aerolínea: «Señorita, por favor, deme la ventanilla».
translation:
Don Ernesto was eighty-two years old and had never been on a plane. When his granddaughter Laura invited him to spend a few weeks with her in Bogotá, at first he said no. “I'm too old now to go on a plane,” he kept saying. But Laura insisted so much that in the end he agreed.

On the day of the trip he arrived at the airport three hours early, with his best hat and a bag full of food for the journey. During takeoff he didn't let go of the armrest and shut his eyes tight. A very kind flight attendant sat next to him for a moment and explained every noise to him. Little by little, Don Ernesto dared to look out of the window. Below, the mountains looked like wrinkles in a green blanket.

He spent three happy weeks in Bogotá. When Laura took him to the airport to go back home, he said to the airline employee: “Miss, please give me the window seat.”

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A pilot who flies over green mountains
An elderly man's first trip by plane
A family that moves from a town to Bogotá
A young woman who works at an airport
questions.explain: The story follows don Ernesto, who 'nunca se había subido a un avión', on his first flight.

questions.q: How did don Ernesto first react to Laura's invitation?
options: He accepted it with great joy
He asked her to visit him instead
He said he was too old to fly
He wanted to travel there by bus
questions.explain: At first he said no: 'Yo ya estoy muy viejo para montar en avión'.

questions.q: Who helped don Ernesto feel calmer during the flight?
options: His granddaughter Laura
The pilot of the plane
A man in the next seat
A flight attendant
questions.explain: 'Una auxiliar de vuelo muy amable' sat with him and explained every noise.

questions.q: What does don Ernesto's request at the end suggest?
options: He now enjoys looking out while flying
He wants to stay longer in Bogotá
He is still very afraid of flying
He prefers to sit next to the pilot
questions.explain: Asking for 'la ventanilla' shows he now wants to enjoy the view instead of closing his eyes.

topic: the Manila galleons across the Pacific
title: El galeón de Manila
text:
Durante unos doscientos cincuenta años, entre 1565 y 1815, grandes barcos españoles cruzaron el océano Pacífico entre Manila, en las Filipinas, y Acapulco, en el actual México. Se les llamaba galeones de Manila, aunque en México se hicieron famosos con otro nombre: la Nao de China.

Desde Asia, los galeones llevaban productos muy deseados en América y en Europa: seda y porcelana de China, especias y muebles finos. Al llegar a Acapulco, una parte de la carga se vendía en una gran feria, y otra parte viajaba por tierra hasta Veracruz, donde otros barcos la llevaban a España. En el viaje de regreso, los galeones volvían a Asia cargados de plata americana, que en China tenía mucho valor.

El viaje no era fácil. De Manila a Acapulco, los barcos tardaban entre cuatro y seis meses, y muchas veces les faltaban el agua y la comida. Aun así, esta ruta unió por primera vez a Asia, América y Europa con un comercio regular.
translation:
For about two hundred and fifty years, between 1565 and 1815, large Spanish ships crossed the Pacific Ocean between Manila, in the Philippines, and Acapulco, in present-day Mexico. They were called Manila galleons, although in Mexico they became famous under another name: the Nao de China.

From Asia, the galleons carried products that were highly desired in America and Europe: silk and porcelain from China, spices and fine furniture. On arriving in Acapulco, part of the cargo was sold at a big fair, and another part traveled overland to Veracruz, where other ships took it to Spain. On the return trip, the galleons went back to Asia loaded with American silver, which was very valuable in China.

The journey was not easy. From Manila to Acapulco, the ships took between four and six months, and they often ran short of water and food. Even so, this route connected Asia, America and Europe through regular trade for the first time.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: A trade route across the Pacific Ocean
How Acapulco became a modern beach city
The history of silver mining in America
The first Spanish city founded in Asia
questions.explain: The text describes the ships that sailed between Manila and Acapulco for about 250 years.

questions.q: What happened to part of the cargo in Acapulco?
options: It was sent back to Manila
It was sold at a big fair
It was kept for the next year
It was given to the sailors
questions.explain: The text says 'una parte de la carga se vendía en una gran feria'.

questions.q: How long did the trip from Manila to Acapulco take?
options: About two weeks
Exactly one year
Between one and two months
Between four and six months
questions.explain: The ships 'tardaban entre cuatro y seis meses'.

questions.q: Why was the galleon probably called 'la Nao de China' in Mexico?
options: It belonged to the emperor of China
Many of its goods came from China
It sailed to China every month
All its sailors were born in China
questions.explain: The galleons brought 'seda y porcelana de China', so the name came from their cargo.

title: Un país, muchas arepas
text:
Pocas comidas son tan colombianas como la arepa, aunque en Venezuela también es un plato nacional. Es un pan redondo y plano hecho con masa de maíz, y su historia es muy antigua: los pueblos indígenas ya la preparaban mucho antes de la llegada de los españoles. Hoy se come a cualquier hora, desde el desayuno hasta la medianoche.

Lo sorprendente es la cantidad de variedades que existen. En Antioquia, la arepa es blanca, delgada y casi sin sal, y acompaña casi todas las comidas. En la costa Caribe es famosa la arepa de huevo: se fríe una vez, se abre, se le mete un huevo crudo y se vuelve a freír. En Boyacá la prefieren gruesa, un poco dulce y con queso. La arepa de choclo se hace con maíz tierno.

Muchos colombianos discuten sobre cuál es la mejor. Pero casi todos están de acuerdo en algo: una arepa caliente con mantequilla y queso es difícil de superar.
translation:
Few foods are as Colombian as the arepa, although in Venezuela it is also a national dish. It is a round, flat bread made from corn dough, and its history is very old: indigenous peoples were already making it long before the Spanish arrived. Today it is eaten at any time of day, from breakfast until midnight.

What is surprising is how many varieties there are. In Antioquia, the arepa is white, thin and almost unsalted, and it goes with almost every meal. On the Caribbean coast, the arepa de huevo is famous: it is fried once, opened, a raw egg is put inside, and it is fried again. In Boyacá people prefer it thick, a little sweet and with cheese. The arepa de choclo is made with young corn.

Many Colombians argue about which one is the best. But almost all of them agree on one thing: a hot arepa with butter and cheese is hard to beat.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: The arepa came to Colombia from Spain
Colombians eat arepas only for breakfast
The arepa is old and has many local versions
The best arepas are made in Venezuela
questions.explain: The text describes the arepa's long history and its many regional varieties.

questions.q: How is the arepa de huevo prepared?
options: It is fried, filled with an egg and fried again
It is cooked on a grill without any oil
It is boiled in water with salt and butter
It is made with young corn and baked
questions.explain: It 'se fríe una vez, se abre, se le mete un huevo crudo y se vuelve a freír'.

questions.q: What is typical of the arepa from Boyacá?
options: It is white, thin and almost unsalted
It is made with rice instead of corn
It is small, flat and very spicy
It is thick, a little sweet and has cheese
questions.explain: In Boyacá 'la prefieren gruesa, un poco dulce y con queso'.

questions.q: What does 'es difícil de superar' mean in the last sentence?
options: It is hard to cook well at home
It is hard to find something better
It is hard to eat in a hurry
It is hard to find in shops
questions.explain: Almost everyone agrees about this arepa, so the phrase means that few things are better than it.

title: ¿Por qué parpadean las estrellas?
text:
En el desierto de la Tatacoa, en el Huila, muchos turistas pasan la noche mirando el cielo. Lejos de las luces de las ciudades, se ven miles de estrellas, y muchas parecen parpadear, como si alguien las encendiera y las apagara muy rápido.

Pero las estrellas no cambian de brillo tan rápido; el responsable es el aire. Antes de llegar a nuestros ojos, la luz de una estrella atraviesa la atmósfera, formada por capas de aire con diferentes temperaturas que se mueven sin parar. Cada capa desvía un poco la luz, y por eso la estrella parece temblar. Como las estrellas están tan lejos que las vemos como puntos diminutos, cualquier movimiento del aire se nota mucho.

Los planetas, en cambio, están mucho más cerca, y su luz no llega de un solo punto, sino de un disco muy pequeño. Por eso casi no parpadean. Desde el espacio, donde no hay atmósfera, los astronautas ven estrellas que brillan de forma completamente estable.
translation:
In the Tatacoa Desert, in Huila, many tourists spend the night looking at the sky. Far from the lights of the cities, thousands of stars can be seen, and many of them seem to twinkle, as if someone were turning them on and off very quickly.

But stars do not change their brightness that fast; the air is responsible. Before reaching our eyes, a star's light passes through the atmosphere, made up of layers of air at different temperatures that move constantly. Each layer bends the light a little, and that is why the star seems to tremble. Since stars are so far away that we see them as tiny points, any movement of the air is very noticeable.

Planets, on the other hand, are much closer, and their light does not come from a single point, but from a very small disk. That is why they hardly twinkle. From space, where there is no atmosphere, astronauts see stars that shine completely steadily.

questions.q: What does the text mainly explain?
options: The best places in Colombia to go camping
How astronauts live and work in space
How desert temperatures change at night
Why the light of stars seems to tremble
questions.explain: The text explains why many stars seem to 'parpadear' at night.

questions.q: According to the text, what makes stars seem to tremble?
options: Moving layers of air in the atmosphere
Dust that rises from the desert floor
The lights of the nearest cities
Clouds that pass in front of them
questions.explain: Their light crosses 'capas de aire' that 'se mueven sin parar', and each layer bends it a little.

questions.q: What do astronauts see when they look at stars from space?
options: Stars that change color quickly
Stars that look much bigger
Stars that tremble even more
Stars that shine in a steady way
questions.explain: In space, 'donde no hay atmósfera', stars 'brillan de forma completamente estable'.

questions.q: What can be concluded about a bright point in the night sky that does not twinkle?
options: It is probably a very distant star
It is probably a planet
It is probably a very large star
It is probably a cloud lit by the Moon
questions.explain: The text says planets 'casi no parpadean' because their light comes from a small disk.
